contract.threat_model: A developer tool that spawns subprocesses carrying the operator's credentials, writes to a run directory, and executes commands declared in a consuming project's CLAUDE.md. In scope: arbitrary command execution through contract keys or capture.mjs; credential leakage into child processes; escape from the intent sandbox that keeps a node from reading the implementation it is supposed to precede; path traversal through run directories or evidence paths; a node spawning further nodes; source leaving the machine through the external panel. A contract overriding a built-in adapter is trusted like a command it declares, and is named wherever the override runs (ARCHITECTURE.md A-26). A link already standing below a run directory, or below another root the owner is given, is in scope; ARCHITECTURE.md A-30 owns which operations are held to it and how. A link swapped in between a check and an open, by a process that can already write the run directory, is a named residual. Out of scope: network listeners, authentication, multi-tenancy, transport security — this process serves nothing and listens on nothing.
